name: Primitive Geometry and Distribution
text:
# Primitive Geometry and Distribution

Also called: Primitive Representation Family

## Overview
This family defines the geometric primitives used to represent 3D scenes in differentiable [splatting](#23-splatting.md) methods, extending the standard 3D Gaussian ellipsoid to alternative shapes, distributions, and dimensionalities. It solves the limitations of volumetric Gaussian mixtures, such as ambiguous geometry, poor [mesh extraction](#14720-mesh-extraction.md), and inefficient representation of sharp edges or opaque surfaces, by introducing planar disks, fat-tailed distributions, [generalized exponential functions](#4663-generalized-exponential-transfer-function.md), and polyhedral volumes [S1, S2, S3]. It differs from sibling methods by varying the fundamental density function or geometric support of the primitive while maintaining the core splatting pipeline of projection and alpha [compositing](#2436-compositing.md).

## Shared principles
All child methods share the core requirement of defining a 3D primitive with a position, orientation, scale, and appearance attributes [G]. The standard 3D Gaussian primitive is defined by a mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ for position, a covariance $\Sigma$ for shape and orientation, and appearance attributes like [Spherical Harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) coefficients and opacity $\alpha$ [G]. Parameterized as $\Sigma^w = R S S^T R^T$ in world space, where $R$ is rotation and $S$ is scaling [G]. The rendering pipeline projects these 3D primitives to 2D screen space [G]. The covariance transforms via the view matrix $W$ and projection Jacobian $J$: $\Sigma = J W \Sigma^w W^T J^T$ [G]. The integral of the 3D density along the view direction yields the [2D splat](#6068-2d-gaussian-splatting.md) density [G].

## Subtopics

### [Direct Gaussian Splatting](3555-direct-gaussian-splatting.md)
[Direct Gaussian Splatting](#3555-direct-gaussian-splatting.md) (dGS) is a method for N-dimensional splatting that replaces the covariance-derived conditioning step of standard [N-DGS](#1774-n-dimensional-gaussian-splatting-n-dgs.md) with explicit per-primitive parameters, removing the need for per-primitive matrix inversions and regression products during rendering. It solves the computational bottleneck of recovering conditional mean, opacity, and covariance from a joint distribution by directly parameterizing the opacity precision and position regression operator. Unlike N-DGS, which couples position and opacity through shared covariance blocks requiring expensive linear algebra, dGS separates these effects using a Cholesky precision factor for opacity and a factorized query-to-position regression operator with learnable per-dimension coupling. It differs from sibling methods like [3D Student's t Distribution Splatting](4352-3d-student-s-t-distribution-splatting.md), [Generalized Exponential Splatting](4684-generalized-exponential-splatting.md), and [2D Gaussian Splatting](6068-2d-gaussian-splatting.md) by explicitly parameterizing the conditioning step rather than deriving it from a joint covariance matrix. See [Direct Gaussian Splatting](3555-direct-gaussian-splatting.md) for implementation details.

### [3D Student's t Distribution Splatting](4352-3d-student-s-t-distribution-splatting.md)
[3D Student's t Distribution Splatting](#4352-3d-student-s-t-distribution-splatting.md) (SSS) is a [neural rendering](#6800-neural-rendering.md) method that replaces the 3D Gaussian primitives of [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) with flexible Student's t distributions and extends the splatting scheme to include both positive (splatting) and negative (scooping) density components. It solves the expressivity limitations of Gaussian mixtures by utilizing fat-tailed distributions and non-monotonic density modeling, achieving higher parameter efficiency (reducing component counts by up to 82%) while maintaining or improving rendering quality. SSS replaces monotonic Gaussian mixtures with Student's t distributions and employs Stochastic Gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (SGHMC) to prevent the degree of freedom parameter $\nu$ from collapsing to local minima. See [3D Student's t Distribution Splatting](4352-3d-student-s-t-distribution-splatting.md) for implementation details.

### [Generalized Exponential Splatting](4684-generalized-exponential-splatting.md)
[Generalized Exponential Splatting](#4684-generalized-exponential-splatting.md) (GES) is a 3D scene representation method that replaces the Gaussian basis functions of 3D Gaussian Splatting with Generalized Exponential Functions (GEF). It introduces a learnable shape parameter $\beta$ for each primitive to better model signals with sharp edges and high-frequency content, reducing the number of particles required and thus memory footprint while maintaining competitive rendering quality. Unlike standard Gaussian Splatting, which assumes low-pass characteristics, GES allows primitives to adapt their shape to fit high-bandwidth signals like squares and triangles more efficiently. See [Generalized Exponential Splatting](4684-generalized-exponential-splatting.md) for implementation details.

### [2D Gaussian Splatting](6068-2d-gaussian-splatting.md)
2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) is a surface reconstruction technique that replaces the volumetric 3D Gaussian ellipsoids of 3D Gaussian Splatting with oriented, zero-thickness 2D disks (surfels). It solves the problem of ambiguous geometry and poor mesh extraction inherent in volumetric representations by aligning primitives with local surface tangent planes, thereby improving multi-view depth consistency and enabling high-resolution normal map recovery. Unlike its sibling [Direct Gaussian Splatting](3555-direct-gaussian-splatting.md), which retains volumetric blobs, 2DGS uses planar primitives to provide unambiguous normals and accurate surface intersection. See [2D Gaussian Splatting](6068-2d-gaussian-splatting.md) for implementation details.

#### LinPrim Octahedron Representation
- **Definition**: A scene representation using transparent polyhedra (octahedra) bounded by triangular faces with homogeneous density, optimized for [differentiable volumetric rendering](#775-differentiable-volumetric-rendering-dvr.md) [S1].
- **Steps**: Restrict vertex positions to lie on the coordinate axes relative to the center to prevent degenerate cases and non-triangular faces [S1]. Enforce symmetry by choosing a single distance to describe opposing corners, so each pair of opposite vertices shares the same distance from the center [S1]. Optimize a rotation quaternion for each primitive to allow arbitrary orientation in space [S1].
- **Parameters**: Octahedra memory requirement is 11 floats per primitive (omitting color), comprising center, rotation, corner distances, and opacity [S1]. Spherical Harmonics (SH) coefficients are 48 floats per primitive (Degree 2), stored to capture view-dependent appearance [S1].

#### High-Opacity Gaussians
- **Definition**: A modification where regular capped Gaussian primitives are converted to high-opacity Gaussians to boost modeling of opaque surfaces with fewer primitives [S2].
- **Steps**: Replace the opacity activation function with `abs()` and clamp blending weights to 1 from above during rendering [S2].
- **Parameters**: Activation switch point is the midpoint of training, specifically 15K iterations [S2].

#### Volumetric Shading System (VSS)
- **Definition**: A method that represents opaque objects with Gaussian density distribution to make the visibility function differentiable, suitable for generative pose estimation [S3].
- **Pitfalls**: VSS is hard to handle geometry with high frequency such as sharp corners, and the rendered image is blurry compared with traditional rendering methods [S3].

## Background
The concept of using explicit geometric primitives for [differentiable rendering](#16276-differentiable-rendering.md) has evolved from [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) to explicit point-based representations. The LinPrim method, introduced in "LinPrim: [Linear Primitives for Differentiable Volumetric Rendering](#2195-linprim-differentiable-rendering-pipeline.md)" (2025), proposed transparent polyhedra like octahedra to replace Gaussian blobs, aiming for [real-time volumetric rendering](#2057-ray-marching-with-single-scattering.md) with linear primitives [S1]. The High-Opacity Gaussian modification, described in "[Taming 3DGS](#8058-taming-3dgs.md): High-Quality Radiance Fields with Limited Resources" (2024), optimized the standard 3DGS pipeline by converting primitives to high-opacity states to better model opaque surfaces [S2]. The Volumetric Shading System (VSS), referenced in "Jrender: An efficient differentiable rendering library based on Jittor" (2023), was an early approach using Gaussian density for visibility functions, though noted for blurring high-frequency geometry [S3].
